source.text: Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν· Πάτερ, ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα· δόξασόν σου τὸν υἱόν, ἵνα ὁ υἱὸς δοξάσῃ σέ, καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκός, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ δώσῃ αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: These things spoke Jesus, and having lifted up the eyes of him to the heaven he said, "Father, has come the hour; glorify of you the Son, that the Son may glorify you, \v 2 just as you gave him authority of all flesh, that all that you have given him he may give to them life eternal.

en.L: Jesus spoke these things, and having lifted up {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes to heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son may glorify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \v 2 just as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority over all flesh, so that all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give eternal life.
en.B: After Jesus had said these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} eyes toward heaven and prayed: "Father, the hour has come. Glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son may glorify {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \v 2 For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} authority over all people, in order that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} may give eternal life to everyone {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: When Jesus had finished saying these things, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked up toward heaven and prayed. He said, "Father, the hour has come. Bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Son, so that the Son can bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \v 2 You have put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in charge of all people. You did this so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could give eternal life to all the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu đã nói những điều này, rồi ngước mắt lên trời, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến; xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con tôn vinh Cha, \v 2 như Cha đã ban cho Con quyền trên mọi xác thịt, để tất cả những gì Cha đã ban cho Con, Con ban cho họ sự sống đời đời.
vi.B: Sau khi nói những điều này, Đức Giê-xu ngước mắt lên trời và cầu nguyện: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến. Xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con tôn vinh Cha. \v 2 Vì Cha đã ban cho Con quyền trên mọi người, để Con ban sự sống đời đời cho tất cả những người Cha đã giao cho Con.
vi.R: Khi Đức Giê-xu nói xong những điều này, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ngước nhìn lên trời và cầu nguyện. Ngài nói: "Lạy Cha, giờ đã đến. Xin Cha tôn vinh Con của Cha, để Con cũng tôn vinh Cha. \v 2 Cha đã giao cho Con quyền trên mọi người. Cha làm vậy để Con ban sự sống đời đời cho tất cả những người Cha đã giao cho Con.

decisions.choice: the hour: the appointed time of Jesus's death and glorification, which has now arrived
alternatives: a period of time in general
decisions.reason: Through the Gospel Jesus's hour had not yet come (2:4; 7:30; 8:20). At 12:23 he said that it had come, and at 13:1 John calls it the hour to pass from this world to the Father. Here, at the start of his prayer, Jesus says it again to the Father: the cross, resurrection and return to the Father are at hand.

decisions.choice: glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you: the Father shows the Son's glory in the hour, and in that same event the Son shows the Father's
decisions.reason: Glorify is a key term. In John, Jesus is glorified when he is lifted up on the cross, raised, and returns to the Father (7:39; 12:23; 13:31-32). The glory of the two is bound together: when the Son is glorified, so is the Father (13:31-32; 14:13). Jesus's first request is not for his own sake alone but so that the Father may be honored.

decisions.choice: so that the Son may glorify you (SBLGNT)
alternatives: so that your Son also may glorify you (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "so that your Son also may glorify you", adding "also" and "your", which repeats the wording of the first request. The older manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, have the shorter text. The meaning is the same either way. A footnote gives the longer reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: authority over all flesh: authority over all human beings
decisions.reason: "All flesh" is a Hebrew way of speaking of all humankind, or of all living things (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:5; Joel 2:28). Here the purpose clause that follows shows that people are meant: the authority is given so that the Son may give life. Compare the authority given to the Son to judge (5:27) and the Father giving all things into his hand (3:35).

decisions.choice: all that you have given him ... to them: the people given to the Son, seen first as one whole and then as persons
alternatives: all things that you have given him (things, not people)
decisions.reason: πᾶν ὃ is neuter, "all that": John speaks of all whom the Father gives as a single gift, as in 6:37 and 6:39. The sentence then turns to the plural masculine "to them", the persons who make up that gift. The neuter phrase stands first for emphasis and is taken up by "to them".

decisions.choice: just as: the gift of authority is the ground of the request
decisions.reason: καθὼς can compare ("just as") or give a reason ("since"). Here it does both: the Son asks to be glorified in keeping with what the Father has already given him, authority over all people, which has eternal life as its purpose.

decisions.choice: you, your, yours, yourself (to the Father); he, him, his, me, my (of the Son); in the whole prayer
decisions.reason: In this prayer Jesus speaks to the Father, so every "you" and "your" addressed to him uses the deity_pronoun setting, and so does every "me" and "my" with which Jesus speaks of himself and every "he" or "him" for the Son, as in 11:41-42. Plain "You" and "He" stand at the start of a sentence. The prayer runs to 17:26, so the quotation opened here does not close in this passage.

decisions.choice: all flesh, all that (L); all people, everyone (B); all people, all the people (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom and the neuter. Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (meaning decision m4) and use words for people where the Greek neuter means people (meaning decision m5), as 6:37 does. "All people" and "everyone" are already inclusive, so they need no gender setting.

decisions.choice: prayed (B, R); Bring glory to; put him in charge of; You did this so that
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that what follows is a prayer, says "bring glory to" (as at 12:28), which keeps the key term in everyday speech, and splits the long sentence. "Hour" stays at every level, as at 12:23, so the thread through the Gospel stays visible.

decisions.choice: "Cha" for the Father and "Con" for Jesus himself, with no setting spans, through the whole prayer
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for John 17, Jesus speaks to the Father as a son to his father: he says "Cha" where the Greek has "you" and "Con" for "I", "me" and "the Son". Both are capitalised nouns and take no deity_pronoun setting, where the English has one on every pronoun.

decisions.choice: phán (L); cầu nguyện (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Phán", the respectful verb for the speech of God or of Jesus, introduces the prayer at Literal; Balanced and Readable say what the words are, a prayer, as the English does.

source.text: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ ἵνα γινώσκωσι σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν θεὸν καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλας Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.

records.literal_gloss: This and is the eternal life, that they may know you the only true God and whom you sent, Jesus Christ.

en.L: And this is eternal life, that they may know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God, and [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: And eternal life is this: that they know {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God, and the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: Eternal life means knowing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the only true God. It means knowing the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent, Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

vi.L: Và đây là sự sống đời đời: là họ biết Cha, Đức Chúa Trời thật duy nhất, và [Đấng] Cha đã sai, Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.B: Và sự sống đời đời là đây: được biết Cha, Đức Chúa Trời thật và duy nhất, và biết Đấng Cha đã sai đến, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.
vi.R: Sự sống đời đời là được biết Cha, là Đức Chúa Trời thật duy nhất. Đó cũng là được biết Đấng Cha đã sai đến, là Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}.

decisions.choice: this is eternal life, that: the clause says what eternal life is
alternatives: this leads to eternal life, that they know
decisions.reason: "This" points forward to the clause that follows, which explains it, as in 6:29, 6:40 and 15:12. Eternal life is not only something that knowing God leads to; knowing God is what it consists of. Verse 2 spoke of the Son giving eternal life; this verse says what that life is.

decisions.choice: know: an ongoing, personal knowing, the knowing of a relationship
decisions.reason: γινώσκωσι is present tense: knowing that goes on, not a single act of learning. In the Bible to know God is to be in a living relationship with him, not only to know facts about him (Jeremiah 31:34; Hosea 6:6). Jesus speaks of the shepherd and the sheep knowing each other, as he and the Father know each other (10:14-15).

decisions.choice: the only true God, and the one he sent: the one God, known together with the Son he sent
decisions.reason: "The only true God" holds to the confession of Israel that there is one God (Deuteronomy 6:4; compare 5:44). Beside him stands the one he sent, and knowing the Son belongs to the same eternal life. John keeps both truths together: there is one God, and the Son is with God and is God (1:1, 18; 10:30).

decisions.choice: Jesus Christ: Jesus names himself in the third person, with the full name, in the prayer
alternatives: Jesus's own words, a solemn naming of himself
John's own wording of the prayer
decisions.reason: The full name "Jesus Christ" occurs in this Gospel only here and at 1:17, and nowhere else does Jesus use it of himself. It is the way believers spoke of him after the resurrection. It may be that John, in giving the prayer, puts it in the words the church used, or Jesus may speak of himself in this solemn way as the one the Father sent. The text does not settle which. Christ is a title, "anointed one" (1:41).

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 1:17, the title follows the name with the christos setting. The name stays at the end, as in the Greek, so the sentence closes on it.

decisions.choice: Eternal life means knowing ... It means knowing
decisions.reason: Readable uses "knowing" to show that the knowing goes on (meaning decision m2), and says it twice so the reader sees that the Son is known together with the Father (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}} at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for the title with the name. Vietnamese needs no article, so the same span serves all three levels.

decisions.choice: Đức Chúa Trời thật
decisions.reason: The guide keeps "chân lý" for the noun "truth" and uses "thật" for the adjective "true", as in "ánh sáng thật".

source.text: ἐγώ σε ἐδόξασα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὸ ἔργον τελειώσας ὃ δέδωκάς μοι ἵνα ποιήσω·

records.literal_gloss: I you glorified on the earth, the work having completed that you have given me that I should do.

en.L: I glorified {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on the earth, having completed the work which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.
en.B: I have glorified {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} on earth by completing the work that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.
en.R: I have brought glory to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} here on earth. I have finished the work {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to do.

vi.L: Con đã tôn vinh Cha trên đất, khi đã hoàn tất công việc Cha đã giao cho Con làm.
vi.B: Con đã tôn vinh Cha trên đất bằng cách hoàn tất công việc Cha giao cho Con làm.
vi.R: Con đã tôn vinh Cha ở dưới đất này. Con đã làm xong công việc Cha giao cho Con.

decisions.choice: Jesus glorified the Father by doing the work the Father gave him
decisions.reason: Jesus's whole life has shown who the Father is: his signs revealed God's glory (2:11; 11:4, 40), and his words were the Father's (12:49-50). He has said from the start that his food is to do the will of the one who sent him and to finish his work (4:34), and that his works bear witness that the Father sent him (5:36). The "I" is emphatic: this is what the Son has done; verse 5 asks what the Father will do.

decisions.choice: having completed: the work is spoken of as done, though the cross is still ahead
alternatives: the work of teaching only, apart from the cross
decisions.reason: τελειώσας is an aorist participle: the Son has brought the work to its goal. As in 13:31, Jesus speaks from the hour itself, so the cross that completes the work is counted with it. "On earth" sets this beside verse 5, where he asks for glory in the Father's presence.

decisions.choice: a link with Jesus's last word on the cross, "It is finished" (19:30)
decisions.reason: On the cross Jesus says Τετέλεσται (19:30), a closely related verb, and John uses this verb for the completing of Scripture just before (19:28). The work he says here is complete is the one he declares finished there. John does not mark the link, so it is noted as likely, not certain.

decisions.choice: have glorified ... by completing (B); have brought glory to ... I have finished (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows by "by" how the Father was glorified (meaning decision m1). Readable says "brought glory to" as elsewhere in the prayer and makes the two parts two sentences.

source.text: καὶ νῦν δόξασόν με σύ, πάτερ, παρὰ σεαυτῷ τῇ δόξῃ ᾗ εἶχον πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι παρὰ σοί.

records.literal_gloss: And now glorify me you, Father, with yourself with the glory which I was having before the the world to be with you.

en.L: And now, Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, with the glory which I had with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before the world existed.
en.B: So now, Father, glorify {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side, with the glory that was {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before there was a world.
en.R: So now, Father, bring glory to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} side. Give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the glory I had with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} before the world began.

vi.L: Và bây giờ, lạy Cha, xin chính Cha tôn vinh Con ở bên Cha, bằng vinh quang mà Con đã có ở bên Cha trước khi có thế gian.
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, lạy Cha, xin chính Cha tôn vinh Con ở bên cạnh Cha, bằng vinh quang Con đã có với Cha trước khi thế gian có mặt.
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, lạy Cha, xin tôn vinh Con ở bên Cha. Xin ban cho Con vinh quang Con đã có với Cha trước khi thế gian được tạo dựng.

decisions.choice: glorify me with yourself: in the Father's own presence, by the Father himself
alternatives: in your sight, in your judgment
decisions.reason: "And now" turns from what the Son has done on earth (verse 4) to what he asks the Father to do. The "you" is emphatic: the Father himself is to glorify him. "With yourself" means beside the Father, in his presence, set against "on earth" in verse 4. Jesus is asking to return to where he came from (13:3; 16:28).

decisions.choice: the glory I had with you before the world existed: the Son shared the Father's glory before creation
alternatives: the glory planned for him before the world, not yet his
decisions.reason: The Son speaks of a glory he had with the Father before the world existed, which fits what John says at the start: in the beginning the Word was with God and was God (1:1-2), and all things came into being through him (1:3). The imperfect "I had" describes a lasting state. In Isaiah God says that he gives his glory to no other (Isaiah 42:8), yet the Son had this glory with him. The verse asks for that glory now, in the Father's presence; it does not say that the Son ever stopped being who he was. Compare 17:24.

decisions.choice: the world: the created order
decisions.reason: Here the world is the whole creation, as in 1:10a and 17:24: the glory was there before anything was made.

decisions.choice: yourself, at your side, was mine (B); at your side, Give me the glory I had (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the emphatic "you" with "yourself" and says "at your side" for the Father's presence (meaning decision m1). Readable splits the request and says "before the world began", plainer than "existed"; Balanced says "before there was a world".

source.text: Ἐφανέρωσά σου τὸ ὄνομα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις οὓς ἔδωκάς μοι ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.

records.literal_gloss: I made manifest of you the name to the men whom you gave me out of the world.

en.L: I revealed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to the {{gender:people|men}} whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} out of the world.
en.B: I have made {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name known to the {{gender:people|men}} {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the world.
en.R: I have shown who {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are to the {{gender:people|men}} {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from the world.

vi.L: Con đã bày tỏ danh Cha cho những người Cha đã ban cho Con từ thế gian.
vi.B: Con đã cho những người Cha ban cho Con từ thế gian biết danh Cha.
vi.R: Con đã cho những người Cha ban cho Con từ thế gian biết Cha là ai.

decisions.choice: your name: the Father himself, as he has made himself known
alternatives: a particular new name for God
decisions.reason: In the Bible a name stands for the person as he has shown himself to be. God made his name known to Moses at the bush (Exodus 3:14-15) and proclaimed it on the mountain, as the God who is merciful and gracious, rich in steadfast love and faithfulness (Exodus 34:5-7). Jesus has made the Father known in the same way: whoever has seen him has seen the Father (1:18; 14:9). Compare 12:28 and 17:26.

decisions.choice: revealed: made visible, brought into the open
decisions.reason: Ἐφανέρωσά means to make visible what was hidden. John uses it of Jesus being revealed to Israel (1:31) and of his glory shown in his signs (2:11). The Father has been shown in what Jesus has said and done.

decisions.choice: whom you gave me out of the world: the disciples, given by the Father and taken from the world
decisions.reason: The people meant are first of all the disciples with Jesus that night. They are the Father's gift to him (6:37, 39; 10:29), and they are taken "out of" the world, the mass of humanity that does not know God (15:19; 17:14-16), while they still live in it (17:11, 15).

decisions.choice: the people: human beings, not men in contrast with women
decisions.reason: The word means human beings. Though the disciples at the table are men, the gift of the Father is spoken of in general terms, and the prayer reaches out to all who will believe (17:20).

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The inclusive "people" is the default and "men" the alternative (meaning decision m4), as at 1:4 and 3:19.

decisions.choice: shown who you are
decisions.reason: Readable says what making the Father's name known means (meaning decision m1), since "your name" alone may sound like only a word.

decisions.choice: những người, with no gender span
alternatives: a gender setting as in the English
decisions.reason: "Người" means a human being of either sex, so the Vietnamese already says what the English gender setting offers; the guide keeps gender spans for "anh chị em".

source.text: σοὶ ἦσαν κἀμοὶ αὐτοὺς ἔδωκας, καὶ τὸν λόγον σου τετήρηκαν.

records.literal_gloss: To you they were, and to me them you gave, and the word of you they have kept.

en.L: They were {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, and to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them, and they have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.
en.B: They belonged to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; they have kept {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.
en.R: They were {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}}, and {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave them to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And they have obeyed {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word.

vi.L: Họ thuộc về Cha, và Cha đã ban họ cho Con, và họ đã giữ lời Cha.
vi.B: Họ vốn thuộc về Cha, và Cha đã giao họ cho Con; họ đã giữ lời Cha.
vi.R: Họ là người của Cha, và Cha đã giao họ cho Con. Họ đã vâng giữ lời Cha.

decisions.choice: they were yours, and you gave them to me: they belonged to the Father before they came to Jesus
decisions.reason: The disciples did not first belong to Jesus and then to God; they were the Father's, and he gave them to the Son (6:37, 44, 65; 10:29). "To me" is emphatic, joined to "and" in one word. The text says that they were the Father's but not how; it does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: kept: held fast to and obeyed
decisions.reason: To keep a word is to hold on to it and do what it says (8:51; 14:23; 15:20). The perfect tense says they have kept it and still do. The disciples will fail Jesus that very night (16:32), but Jesus speaks of their faith as a whole.

decisions.choice: your word: the Father's message, which Jesus spoke
decisions.reason: The word the disciples kept is the Father's, given through Jesus: the word they hear from Jesus is not his own but the Father's who sent him (14:24). Verse 8 speaks of the same thing in the plural, "the words".

decisions.choice: belonged to you (B); obeyed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says "belonged to" for the plain "were yours". Readable says "obeyed", the everyday sense of keeping a word (meaning decision m2), so that "kept your word" is not read as keeping a promise.

source.text: νῦν ἔγνωκαν ὅτι πάντα ὅσα δέδωκάς μοι παρὰ σοῦ εἰσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Now they have known that all things as many as you have given me from you are.

en.L: Now they have known that all things whatever {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} are from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Now they have come to know that all {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Now they understand that all the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} came from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

vi.L: Bây giờ họ đã biết rằng mọi điều Cha đã ban cho Con đều đến từ Cha.
vi.B: Giờ đây họ đã nhận biết rằng mọi điều Cha ban cho Con đều từ Cha mà đến.
vi.R: Bây giờ họ hiểu rằng mọi điều Cha ban cho Con đều đến từ Cha.

decisions.choice: they have known (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read "they have known". A few read "I have known", and a few have other forms of the verb. "They" fits the flow of the prayer, which in verses 6-8 is all about what the disciples have received and believed. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: now they have come to know: a knowing reached and still held
decisions.reason: ἔγνωκαν is perfect tense: they have come to know and now know. "Now" looks back to the last words of the disciples at the supper: "Now we know ... we believe that you came from God" (16:30).

decisions.choice: all you have given me: everything Jesus has, his words and his works, comes from the Father
decisions.reason: What the disciples have come to see is that nothing in Jesus is his own apart from the Father: his words (verse 8; 12:49), his works (5:36), and his authority (17:2). That is the knowing that leads to the faith of verse 8.

decisions.choice: have come to know (B); understand (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows the perfect tense, knowing reached and still held (meaning decision m2). Readable says "understand", the everyday word for knowing of this kind.

source.text: ὅτι τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἔδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλαβον καὶ ἔγνωσαν ἀληθῶς ὅτι παρὰ σοῦ ἐξῆλθον, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.

records.literal_gloss: Because the words which you gave me I have given to them, and they received and knew truly that from you I came out, and they believed that you me sent.

en.L: For the words which {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I have given to them, and they received [them] and knew truly that from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I came out, and they believed that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: For I have passed on to them the words {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they have accepted them. They have come to know for certain that I came from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and they believe that it was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: This is because I gave them the words {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and they accepted them. They know for sure that I came from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and they believe that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

vi.L: Vì những lời Cha đã ban cho Con, Con đã ban cho họ, và họ đã nhận [những lời ấy] và đã biết thật rằng Con từ Cha mà ra, và họ đã tin rằng Cha đã sai Con.
vi.B: Vì Con đã truyền lại cho họ những lời Cha ban cho Con, và họ đã đón nhận. Họ đã biết chắc rằng Con từ Cha mà đến, và họ tin rằng chính Cha đã sai Con.
vi.R: Đó là vì Con đã trao cho họ những lời Cha ban cho Con, và họ đã nhận những lời ấy. Họ biết chắc Con đến từ Cha, và họ tin rằng Cha là Đấng đã sai Con.

decisions.choice: for: this explains how the disciples came to know (verse 7)
decisions.reason: ὅτι here gives the reason for verse 7: they know that everything Jesus has comes from the Father because he gave them the Father's words, and they received them.

decisions.choice: the words: the sayings Jesus spoke, all of which came from the Father
decisions.reason: The plural ῥήματα means the things Jesus said one by one; the singular "word" in verse 6 is the message as a whole. Jesus has said that he speaks only what the Father told him (12:49-50; 14:10). John uses the plural for the words that give life (6:63, 68).

decisions.choice: knew truly: came to know with real certainty
decisions.reason: ἀληθῶς means "truly" or "in truth": their knowing is real and sure. The aorist tenses (received, knew, believed) speak of what happened when they took in Jesus's words.

decisions.choice: I came from you ... you sent me: Jesus's origin with the Father and his mission from him
decisions.reason: Two ways of saying the same truth: Jesus came out from the Father, and the Father sent him. The disciples said just this at 16:30 ("we believe that you came from God"), and Jesus answered it at 16:27-28. The "you" in "you sent me" is emphatic: it was the Father, and no other, who sent him. Believing that the Father sent him is what the Gospel asks of everyone (11:42; 17:21; 20:31).

decisions.choice: For I have passed on to them ... it was you who sent me (B); This is because ... you are the one who sent me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the verb first and breaks the long sentence in two. Literal brackets [them], which the Greek leaves understood after "received"; the other levels supply it. Readable says "This is because" to tie the sentence to verse 7 (meaning decision m1) and uses the present "know" and "believe" for knowing and faith that last. Balanced and Readable show the emphatic "you" (meaning decision m4), as 11:42 does.
